tests.scope: Actual ordinary Windows Python 3.12.13 execution; process, SYSTEM boundary, clocks and supervisor timing explicitly simulated in observer fixtures. No physical SYSTEM/48-hour or native heap evidence.

repaired: A fresh measurement after a long pause cannot satisfy continuous 48-hour observation: each completed sample must be within 10 seconds of the prior sample/start on both wall and monotonic clocks. Reversed clocks fail. Default 1-second cadence leaves scheduler headroom; a 10-second requested interval can honestly fail on overhead.
Completion requires a valid observed sample at or beyond 172800 seconds, not merely elapsed time after an interrupted or blocked operation.
Fresh psutil Process objects check creation time before and after sampling so the original cached create_time cannot hide PID reuse.
Each row retains PID, creation time, instance id, both gaps, and the raw external heap used/capacity/time/process/source values. Freshness is checked again after evidence reads.

findings.finding: UOI_HEAPSIZE supplies desktop capacity in KB. No documented used-byte index is provided; capacity alone remains insufficient.

The debugger extension reports per-session/window-station/desktop heap size and displayed used rate. Its rounded-rate precision, current-process association and repeated safe acquisition have not been validated on this host.

Microsoft documents ETW allocation/free/reallocation tracing. This documentation does not establish desktop-heap used/capacity accounting; ordinary process-heap tracing is not accepted as a substitute.

Microsoft documents Win32k event 243 as an allocation-failure warning logged only once per session. The cited article applies to supported Windows Server. This is a potential supplemental failure signal, not a current Windows 11 measured utilization or continuous sampling contract; no eventlog query was run.
The documented kernel-debug route requires Administrator execution; LiveKD snapshots need not represent a single instant. No debugger, dump, tracing session or driver was launched.

remaining.hard_block: No verified supported nonintrusive acquisition route for fresh service-desktop used/capacity evidence is available under the current no-debugger/no-driver/no-boot-change constraints. This is an unresolved acquisition contract, not proof such a method is impossible.
remaining.owner_decision_if_constraint_persists: Either separately review and establish a supported acquisition route and real sample contract, or explicitly amend the desktop-heap acceptance requirement. Counts, RSS, capacity, absence of warnings and rounded-percent multiplication must never be relabeled as actual used bytes. No amendment was made.
future_integration: Include this repository repair in a separately reviewed fresh protected runtime or acceptance package; frozen r3 remains unchanged.
Establish actual service desktop/session and exact Warden PID/creation binding, collector provenance and measurement precision before writing an adapter.
Preserve the strict <15% ceiling and <=10-second freshness; if a conservative rate-bound representation is chosen, review an explicitly labelled schema rather than invent used bytes.

Once Warden/supervisor and the real collector are installed and validated, run the observer with a new protected evidence directory at the default 1-second interval. Missing collector data remains unavailable, never zero.

A completed 48-hour run additionally needs real workload coverage, no process/instance replacement, handle/resource bounds and independent supervisor observation/recovery timing. Synthetic tests do not satisfy those requirements.
